title: The cell cycle and its checkpoints
caption: Interphase (G₁, S and G₂) takes up most of the cycle, and M phase is mitosis and cytokinesis. The cycle can pause at three checkpoints, in G₁, G₂ and at metaphase, until problems are fixed. Cells that stop dividing leave for G₀.
alt: A cycle of four boxes, G1, S, G2 and M, with arrows between them labelled with the G1 and G2 checkpoints and the daughter cells that start the next G1.
description: G₁: the cell grows and carries out its normal functions; the G₁ checkpoint checks size, nutrients, growth signals and DNA damage before S phase.
S: DNA is replicated; DNA content doubles from 2C to 4C.
G₂: the cell makes proteins for division and the G₂ checkpoint checks the DNA has been copied correctly.
M: mitosis, with the spindle checkpoint at metaphase, then cytokinesis; two identical daughter cells return to 2C.
A typical cycle in cultured human cells takes about 24 hours.
